lines.text: You again. You die at the rail, you die in the hold, yet here you stand. What devil walks in your boots?
lines.journalNote: Kedar recognizes me across the loops. His smirk broke into cold, creeping dread.

lines.text: You look tired. Sleep. It's cheap, I hear.
lines.journalNote: First Mate Kedar Voss watches the deck with cold, idle amusement. His hand rests on his dirk.

lines.text: Mind your business at the hatch. Some cargo is strictly between me and my men.
lines.journalNote: Kedar warned me away from the hold. He is rallying men among the brine barrels.

lines.text: Thorne had his turn at the wheel. The Jal-Doot answers to me now. Stay out of my path.
lines.journalNote: Kedar holds the bloody helm. He took the ship and took Thorne's chest keys.

lines.text: Damn the beast! It followed the crystal's hum! Isha, blow that devil back into the trough!
lines.journalNote: Kedar curses the sea beast. He knows the humming stone in the hold drew the Makara to us.

lines.text: A wise man doesn't drown for another man's ledger. Gold buys more loyalty than any commission.
lines.journalNote: Kedar cares only for the hold's locked gold. A purse might stay his blade.

lines.text: Ah, our esteemed Navigator. Keep us off the black reefs, friend. When new hands take the helm, there will be a generous share for a man of your skill.
lines.journalNote: Kedar spoke with smooth, measured politeness. He wants the Navigator alive to steer the ship after the mutiny.

lines.text: Keep your ledger shut and your nose out of the bilge, Quartermaster. Count your coins in silence and don't come sniffing around my business.
lines.journalNote: Kedar warned me away with cold suspicion. He watches the Quartermaster like a hawk.

lines.text: ...Out of my path, boy. A deckhand should be swabbing brine, not gaping at his betters.
lines.journalNote: Kedar waved me away without looking up. To him, a deckhand is just grease on the deck.

lines.text: You look at me like you know something.
lines.journalNote: Kedar eyed me sharply, wondering how much I've pieced together.

lines.text: The old man and his iron box... some fools think numbers will keep their throats dry.
lines.journalNote: Kedar scoffed at the Captain's safe and locks.
